conclusions: A standing scope propagates through the records store into a downstream consumer before the balancing path can react, so scope duration is the control point rather than scope correctness.

conclusions: Three mechanisms are available: accept the standing grant, bound the grant in time, or separate the permission change from the functional change.

structured_payload.label: Merge the change as submitted
structured_payload.mechanism: Accept the widened service account scope and the new configuration handler exactly as written and release inside the current window.
structured_payload.tradeoff: Grants a standing write and secrets-read scope that no rollback removes automatically.

structured_payload.label: Merge with a request-scoped short-lived credential
structured_payload.mechanism: Replace the standing grant with a credential issued per deployment request and expiring at the end of it, keeping the handler otherwise unchanged.
structured_payload.tradeoff: Adds a credential-issuance dependency to every deployment and costs one extra release cycle to implement.

structured_payload.label: Split the change and ship the handler alone
structured_payload.mechanism: Land only the configuration handler behind a feature flag and defer every permission modification to a separate reviewed change.
structured_payload.tradeoff: Leaves the handler inert until a second change lands, so no user-visible value ships in this window.

conclusions: Removing the standing scope is asserted to be safe on the basis of a review that examined only this handler, so the scoped option carries an unquantified regression risk for other consumers.
Merging as submitted bundles an irreversible permission grant with a functional change, which the change-time scan already routes away from automatic acceptance.

structured_payload.remediation: Add a test that asserts the effective credential scope at deployment time, or stop citing the suite as scope evidence.

conclusions: The only irreversible failure mode in this change belongs to merging as submitted, because a standing grant persists after any code rollback.

structured_payload.precondition: No scheduled review removes the grant after this release.
structured_payload.statement: The standing secrets-read scope is never revoked, and a later unrelated change reuses the same service account to reach customer records.

structured_payload.detection_signal: Deployment failures correlate with identity provider latency.
structured_payload.precondition: The identity provider has no fallback issuance path.
structured_payload.statement: Credential issuance becomes a deployment dependency and an issuance outage blocks all releases.

structured_payload.detection_signal: The feature flag remains off for more than two release cycles.
structured_payload.precondition: The follow-up permission change is never scheduled.
structured_payload.statement: The handler ships behind a flag and is forgotten, leaving dead code that later readers assume is active.

conclusions: Bounding the credential in time converts an invisible standing risk into a monitored signal, which compounds in value across later changes.

operators_deferred.detail: Requires a validated source-domain corpus and a structural-mapping check to avoid surface-similarity reasoning. Without a mapping validity test it degrades into decorative comparison, which is precisely the failure mode this system exists to prevent.

Its value is reframing the problem statement, which conflicts with a v0.1 pipeline that treats the intake frame as fixed for the run. Enabling it requires a re-entrant router that can restart classification, which is a v0.2 routing change.
Produces connections whose quality cannot yet be scored deterministically. Admitting unscoreable output into the evidence-weighted convergence would let unweighted material influence a decision.

Deliberately holds opposed propositions simultaneously, which the v0.1 contradiction gate is built to flag and route to REVIEW. Admitting it requires a contradiction taxonomy that distinguishes productive tension from unresolved conflict. That taxonomy is the v0.2 prerequisite.
